summary: Iteration 39 — Frontend-only test of the new DOUGH DIGITAL TWIN tool (Maestro > Passo 4 > maestro-tool-twin) at 430x900 as admin PRO. All rendering and simulation logic verified correct: twin-time/twin-volume/twin-rechyd/twin-alveo/twin-chart/twin-crumb/twin-advice all present; recharts line renders (1 .recharts-line-curve, box 372x180); 13 deterministic crumb bubbles; reactivity correct (temp 24->32: 4h00 -> 2h10; dose 1->3%: 4h00 -> 1h20; hyd 65->95: alveo 'Media' 33/100 -> 'Aperta e irregolare' 87/100; ldb->madre: 4h00 -> 5h00; salt 4%: 5h41; W=400: volume 3.0x, ideal hyd ~92%). No console errors except two expected 401 from /api/auth/me while anonymous. Regression OK: meteo, acqua, ph, termo all open from Passo 4. ONE REAL UX BUG FOUND: the range sliders are remounted on every state change (Slider declared inline inside DoughTwin), so dragging stops after the first step and keyboard arrows only work once.

ui_bugs.component: DoughTwin sliders (all 5: twin-Idratazione, 'twin-Forza W', twin-Temperatura, twin-Dose, twin-Sale)
ui_bugs.issue: Slider input is unmounted/remounted on every re-render, so it loses pointer capture and focus after the FIRST value change. Mouse drag from 30% to 85% of the track only moved 65% -> 70% (value frozen at 70 for the rest of the drag); keyboard test: focus() + ArrowRight moved 24 -> 25 then document.activeElement became null and the 2nd ArrowRight did nothing. Confirmed via DOM identity probe: a marker set on the input node is gone after another state change (node recreated). Users must click repeatedly instead of dragging; a11y/keyboard control is broken.

issues: The floating 'Radio' FAB (bottom-left) overlaps the 'Idratazione ideale' card and partially covers the key value (~68%/~92%) when that card sits at FAB height; the 'Parla' FAB similarly overlaps the Alveolatura card. Pre-existing app-wide FAB overlap, but here it hides simulation output values.
Advice block correctly shows >=1 tip; with default values only 1 tip appears (expected).

action_items: HIGH: move the `Slider` sub-component out of the DoughTwin function body (define it at module scope, e.g. `const Slider = ({label, Icon, value, set, ...}) => (...)` above `export default function DoughTwin`) — because it is redefined on every render React sees a new component type and remounts the <input type=range>, breaking drag and keyboard control.
OPTIONAL (design): ensure the Radio/Parla FABs do not sit on top of the result cards (extra bottom/side padding or hide FABs while a Maestro tool is open).
critical_code_review_comments: DoughTwin.jsx: inline `Slider` component definition inside the render body -> full remount of each range input on every simulation update (root cause of the drag/keyboard bug). Same pattern should be audited in other sections that use inline sliders.
Simulation math is sound and deterministic; useMemo deps are complete; the crumb-bubble PRNG is seeded from score/w/hyd so previews are stable — good.

Slider data-testid derives from the translated label (`twin-${label}`), so testids change with language (twin-Idratazione / twin-Hydratation / twin-Hydration). Prefer a language-independent id (e.g. twin-slider-hyd) for stable automation.

success_rate.frontend: 92% (all rendering + simulation assertions pass; slider drag/keyboard interaction fails)

seed_data_creation: None (tool is pure client-side computation, no API calls).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Flow: init localStorage mikilab_onboarding={done:true,type:'panificio'} + mikilab_seen_intro='1', close [data-testid=intro-close-btn] (appears before AND after login), login via login-btn -> auth-screen, then nav-tab-maestro -> maestro-step-4 -> maestro-tool-twin. Inside a tool the stepper is hidden: to switch tools click the 'Strumenti' back link first. Sliders must be driven with .fill() (drag/keyboard unreliable until the remount bug is fixed).
rca_of_the_issue: The `Slider` arrow function is declared inside the DoughTwin component body, so a fresh component type is created on every render. React therefore unmounts and remounts the underlying <input type='range'> whenever any state changes, destroying focus and pointer capture. Reproduction: open the twin tool, press-and-hold on the hydration slider and drag — the value advances one step then freezes; or focus the temperature slider and press ArrowRight twice — only the first press registers (activeElement becomes null). Fix: hoist Slider to module scope (or wrap with useCallback/React.memo defined outside the component).
